aamu: Basic form. After 'joka' (every) the noun stays in the basic form: joka aamu.
sofia: A name. Names take case endings too: Sofian, Sofialle.
anteeksi: One fixed word for both 'sorry' and 'excuse me'.
apteekki: Basic form: the subject of the sentence.
asema: Basic form: the subject of the sentence.
asun: Verb stem asu- plus -n, the ending for minä (I). The pronoun can be left out.
asut: Verb stem asu- plus -t, the ending for sinä (you).
asuu: For hän the last vowel of the stem doubles: asu- → asuu.
auki: Never changes form: kauppa on auki, kaupat ovat auki.
baariin: Illative (mihin? where to?): the last vowel doubles and -n is added.
bileisiin: bileet is always plural. Plural -i- + illative -siin: into the party.
bussi: Basic form: the subject of the sentence.
bussilla: Adessive -lla marks the vehicle or tool you use: bussilla, junalla, kortilla.
ei: The negative verb for hän. In Finnish 'not' is a verb and takes person endings: en, et, ei.
en: The negative verb with -n for minä. The main verb after it loses its ending: en puhu.
englantia: Partitive -a. Languages you speak are always in the partitive: puhun englantia.
entä: Starts a follow-up question: Entä sinulle? Entä sinä?
espanjaa: Partitive -a. Languages you speak are always in the partitive.
espanjasta: Elative -sta (mistä? from where?): out of a place.
euroa: After any number except one, the noun is in the partitive singular: viisi euroa.
haluaisin: Stem halua- + conditional -isi- (would) + -n (I). The polite way to ask for things.
haluan: haluta is verb type 4: the stem is halua-, then -n for minä.
haluatko: Stem halua- + -t (you) + -ko, which turns the word into a question.
hauska: 'Hauska tutustua' is the set phrase for 'nice to meet you'.
he: Basic form. In speech people say 'ne'.
hei: Neutral greeting, fine everywhere. 'Hei hei' means bye.
helsingissä: Consonant gradation nk → ng in the stem, then inessive -ssä (missä? in).
helsinkiin: Illative (mihin?): vowel doubles + n. The strong grade nk stays.
hitaammin: hidas (slow) → hitaasti (slowly) → hitaammin (more slowly). -mmin makes the comparative.
hitto: A mild swear word, safe almost anywhere.
humalassa: Literally 'in the hop' (humala = hop plant). Inessive -ssa (in).
huomenna: Time word. The old -na ending (when?) also appears in tänään.
huomenta: Short for 'hyvää huomenta'. Greetings and wishes are in the partitive.
hyvää: Partitive -ä. Used in wishes (hyvää päivää), in 'kuuluu hyvää', and to describe uncountable things.
hän: One word for both he and she. Finnish has no grammatical gender.
idiootti: Same word as in English, with a Finnish double t.
ikävä: Minulla on ikävä + partitive = I miss. Literally 'I have a longing'.
ihan: A strengthening word: ihan hyvä (pretty good), ihan paska (total shit).
jatkoille: jatkot is always plural. Plural -i- + allative -lle (onto).
joka: Here 'every'. The noun after it stays in the basic form.
juon: juoda is verb type 2: drop -da, add -n.
juovat: Stem juo- + -vat, the ending for he (they).
juustoa: Partitive -a: an unspecified amount of food or drink.
kahvi: Basic form. 'Yksi kahvi' is one serving, so no partitive.
kahvia: Partitive -a: some coffee, an unspecified amount.
kai: On its own 'kai' means 'probably'. 'Totta kai' is the set phrase for 'of course'.
kaksi: After it the noun is in the partitive singular: kaksi siskoa.
kalaa: Partitive -a: fish as food, an unspecified amount.
kassin: The -n marks a whole, complete object: one bag.
kaukana: An old -na ending answering 'where?'. Compare kaukaa (from far) and kauas (to far).
kauppaan: Illative (mihin?): vowel doubles + n. The strong grade pp stays (but: kaupassa).
kauramaitoa: kaura (oat) + maito (milk) + partitive -a: some oat milk.
kiinni: Never changes form: ravintola on kiinni.
kiitos: Thank you. When ordering it also works as 'please'.
kippis: Said with eye contact before the first sip.
kirjasto: kirja (book) + -sto (a collection of): a place of books.
kirjaston: Genitive -n. Words like vieressä (next to) need the genitive before them.
kortilla: Consonant gradation tt → t in the stem, then adessive -lla (with, by means of).
korvapuusti: korva (ear) + puusti (slap). Nobody is quite sure why.
korvapuustin: The -n marks a whole, complete object: one roll.
kovalla: kova (hard, loud) + adessive -lla. Volume is 'on' a level: kovalla, hiljaisella.
kupin: Consonant gradation pp → p, then -n for a whole object: one cup.
kuuluu: 'Mitä kuuluu?' is literally 'what is heard?'. The vowel doubles for the hän-form.
kyllä: A formal yes. In speech: joo.
kylmää: Partitive -ä: describing something uncountable (milk) puts the adjective in the partitive.
lasi: Basic form. Lasi vettä = a glass of water.
leipää: Partitive -ä: some bread, an unspecified amount.
lihaa: Partitive -a. In a negative sentence the object is always in the partitive.
liian: Before an adjective: liian kallis, liian kylmä.
lipun: Consonant gradation pp → p, then -n for a whole object.
lonkeron: The -n marks a whole, complete object: one drink.
lähellä: Adessive -llä answering 'where?'. Compare läheltä (from near) and lähelle (to near).
maksaa: The hän-form (costs) and the dictionary form (to pay) look the same.
meille: me + -i- + allative -lle: 'to us', which means 'to my/our place'.
mene: The command form for sinä is the bare stem: mene, tule, syö.
menee: Stem mene- with the vowel doubled for hän.
menemme: Stem mene- + -mme, the ending for me (we).
menen: mennä is verb type 3: stem mene- + -n.
mennään: The passive form. It means 'let's go', and in speech also plain 'we go': me mennään.
mennäänkö: The passive 'let's go' + question -kö: shall we go?
mikä: Question word in the basic form.
milloin: Question word. In speech: millon, koska.
minulla: Adessive -lla. Finnish has no verb 'to have': minulla on = 'on me there is'.
minä: Often dropped, because the verb ending already says who. In speech: mä.
miljoonaa: Partitive -a after a number: kolme miljoonaa.
moi: Casual greeting, used with everyone. 'Moi moi' means bye.
missä: The question word in the inessive: literally 'in what?'.
mistä: The question word in the elative: literally 'out of what?'.
mukaan: 'Mukaan' at a café means takeaway. Also 'along with': tule mukaan.
musiikki: Basic form: the subject of the sentence.
mutta: Never changes. Note the double t: 'muta' would be mud.
nimeni: nimi → nime- + possessive suffix -ni (my). With the suffix, 'minun' is optional.
olemme: Stem ole- + -mme (we). In speech: me ollaan.
olen: Stem ole- + -n (I). In speech: mä oon.
olet: Stem ole- + -t (you). In speech: sä oot.
oletko: olet + -ko, which turns it into a question. The verb moves to the front.
olla: Dictionary form. 'Mitä saisi olla?' = what may it be?
olut: Basic form. 'Yksi olut' is one serving, so no partitive.
omenan: The -n marks a whole, complete object: one apple.
on: The hän-form of olla. Irregular, so just memorise it.
onko: on + question ending -ko: is it…? With -lla it asks about having: onko sinulla lippu?
opiskelen: opiskella is verb type 3: opiskel- + e + -n.
opiskelijoita: opiskelija + plural -i- + partitive -ta. After 'olla' a plural group is in the partitive.
ostan: Verb type 1: drop the final -a, add -n.
otan: Consonant gradation tt → t in the stem, then -n.
ovat: The he-form of olla. Irregular. In speech: ne on.
paljon: The noun after it goes in the partitive: paljon kahvia.
pankki: Basic form. With endings: pankissa (kk → k).
paska: Noun and adjective: paska päivä (a shit day).
pekka: A name. With endings it follows gradation: Pekan, Pekalle.
perkele: An old word for the devil. Roll the R.
puhu: After the negative verb the main verb is the bare stem: en puhu, et puhu, ei puhu.
puhua: Dictionary form, needed after voida (can): voitko puhua.
puhutko: puhut + question -ko. Finnish has no 'do': the verb itself becomes the question.
rakastan: Verb type 1 + -n. Its object is always in the partitive.
ravintola: ravinto (nutrition) + -la (place of). Same -la as in kahvila.
ruotsia: Partitive -a. Languages you speak are always in the partitive.
saanko: saada (to get, to be allowed) + -n (I) + question -ko.
saisi: saada + conditional -isi-. 'Mitä saisi olla?' is how staff ask what you would like.
se: It. In speech 'se' is also used for people instead of hän.
sinua: Partitive -a. rakastaa and suudella take a partitive object.
sinulla: Adessive -lla: onko sinulla = do you have.
sinusta: Elative -sta, because tykätä always takes -sta: tykkään sinusta.
sinä: One person, informal. Used with almost everyone. In speech: sä.
siskoa: After any number except one, the noun is in the partitive singular: kaksi siskoa.
sovelluksesta: Words ending in -us change to -ukse- before endings. Elative -sta (from).
sori: A loan from English. Lighter than anteeksi.
suomalainen: -lainen makes a person from a place: espanjalainen, turkulainen.
suomalaiset: Words in -nen change to -se- before endings. The -t is the basic plural.
saunaa: Partitive singular after a number, even though English uses a plural.
suomea: suomi → suome- + partitive -a. Languages you speak are in the partitive.
suomi: Lower case is the language, capital S is the country.
suudella: Dictionary form, needed after saanko (may I).
syö: After the negative verb the main verb is the bare stem: en syö.
syön: syödä is verb type 2: drop -dä, add -n.
syötkö: syöt + question -kö. It is -kö, not -ko, because of vowel harmony with ö.
tanssia: Dictionary form, needed after haluta (to want).
tarvitsetko: tarvita is verb type 5: the stem is tarvitse-. Then -t (you) + question -ko.
teetä: Partitive. After a long vowel the ending is -ta/-tä instead of -a/-ä.
teille: te + -i- + allative -lle: 'to you', which means 'to your place'.
teillä: te (plural or polite you) + adessive -llä: onko teillä = do you have.
tervetuloa: terve (healthy, also a greeting) + tuloa (arrival, in the partitive).
tori: Basic form. The heart of every Finnish town.
totta: Partitive of tosi (true). 'Totta kai' = of course.
treffeille: treffit is always plural: treffe- + plural -i- + allative -lle (onto).
tulee: tulla is verb type 3: stem tule-, vowel doubles for hän.
turku: Basic form. Finland's oldest city. In Swedish: Åbo.
turkuun: Illative (mihin?): vowel doubles + n. The strong grade rk stays.
turussa: Consonant gradation: the k disappears (rk → r), then inessive -ssa.
tutustua: Dictionary form. 'Hauska tutustua' = nice to meet you.
tykkään: tykätä is verb type 4: the stem is tykkää- (strong kk), then -n. Its object takes -sta.
täällä: tämä (this) in the adessive: at this place.
töihin: työ → plural stem töi- + illative -hin. Literally 'into works'.
vai: 'Or' in questions where you must choose. In statements 'or' is tai.
vanha: Basic form. Age: kymmenen vuotta vanha.
vanhin: vanha (old) → vanhin (oldest). The ending -in makes the superlative.
vettä: vesi → vet- + partitive -tä: some water. One of the classic irregular stems.
vieressä: A postposition: it comes after the noun, which must be in the genitive: kirjaston vieressä.
vihainen: viha (anger) + -inen, the ending that makes adjectives.
vittu: The strongest and most versatile Finnish swear word.
vitun: Consonant gradation tt → t, then genitive -n. The genitive of a swear works as an intensifier.
voi: An exclamation here. 'Voi' is also butter, and 'he/she can'.
vuotta: vuosi → vuot- + partitive -ta, because it follows a number.
vähän: The noun after it goes in the partitive: vähän suomea.
väsynyt: From väsyä (to get tired): 'having tired'. In speech: väsyny.
yksi: After 'yksi' the noun stays in the basic form: yksi kahvi.
yliopistolle: Allative -lle: to the university as a destination or campus.
ymmärrä: After the negative verb comes the bare stem. Gradation rt → rr: ymmärtää → en ymmärrä.
ystäviä: ystävä + plural -i- + partitive -ä. After 'olla' a plural group is in the partitive.
ole: The form after the negative verb: ei ole = is not.
maa: Basic form. Also means land, ground and earth.
kieltä: kieli → kiel- + partitive -tä. After a number from two up, the noun is partitive.
yliopistoa: Partitive -a, because of the number kaksi before it.
keskustaan: Illative: the last vowel doubles, then -n.
aino: A name. Names take endings too: Ainon, Ainolle.
mikko: A name. Names take endings too: Mikon, Mikolle.
yhdysvalloista: Yhdysvallat is plural (it ends in -t), so the ending goes on the plural stem: Yhdysvallo- + -i- + -sta.
englanti: Basic form. Languages are written lowercase.
espanja: Basic form. The country is capitalised; the language, espanja, is not.
helsinki: Basic form. With endings the nk changes: Helsingissä.
kortti: Basic form. With some endings the tt becomes t: kortilla.
pysäkki: Basic form. With some endings the kk becomes k: pysäkillä.
ruotsi: Basic form. The country Sweden is Ruotsi, with a capital.
yhdysvallat: Basic form. It is plural: literally “the united states”.
